mainTopic: Explaining the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about rejecting the other side's judge and witnesses, and how it relates to the rule of צריך לברר
overview: The גמרא first explains why the argument between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about backing out of an agreement appears in two משניות. Each case could have made us think one side agrees with the other. It then challenges רב דימי's reading, because the משנה says 'his witnesses' in the plural. רבי אלעזר says instead that the litigant and another person come to disqualify the other side's witnesses. After the objection that the litigant is נוגע בעדותו, the גמרא explains that he is challenging the witness's family lineage. רבי מאיר accepts this as indirect testimony, and the רבנן reject it. רב דימי then reports רבי יוחנן's view: the dispute is about two sets of witnesses and depends on whether one must prove the witnesses he claims to have (צריך לברר). The גמרא asks whether this matches the argument between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about a שטר and a חזקה. It concludes that the two arguments are not the same, because a חזקה depends on the שטר while separate sets of witnesses do not depend on each other. Finally, רבין begins a different report of what רבי יוחנן said, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב דימי: The case is where he accepted just one
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains that the משנה's case is one where the litigant agreed to rely on a single person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב דימי, son of רב נחמן, son of רב יוסף, said: This is a case where he accepted it upon himself with one person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי explains the case in the משנה. He says the litigant had agreed to rely on just one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you cannot simply reject the other side's valid witnesses. רב דימי limits the משנה to a case where the litigant had agreed to rely on one person, which is not the normal standard. Because he only agreed to it, he might be able to take that agreement back.

keyTerms.meaning: Such as / this is a case where
He accepted him upon himself (he agreed to rely on him)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב דִּימִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
phrases.english: And Rav Dimi, son of Rav Nachman, said
son of Rav Yosef:
Such as where he accepted it upon himself with one.
phrases.notes: He means he agreed to accept one witness as if he were two, as the next lines explain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב דִּימִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of how one side can reject the other side's judge or witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה is speaking about a litigant who agreed to rely on a single person, so the case depends on his own agreement.

steps.title: Both cases are needed: the 'father' case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that if we only had the next משנה's case of 'my father' or 'your father', we might think the רבנן agree with רבי מאיר in the case of one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If the משנה had only taught 'my father' and 'your father', we would say that only there do the רבנן rule that he cannot back out, because a father is fit to judge for the general public. But one witness counting as two is not fit for the general public, so you might say the רבנן agree with רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The same argument also appears in the next משנה, so the גמרא explains why we need it taught twice. This step gives the first half: why the 'father' case alone is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the next משנה, the רבנן say a person cannot back out after accepting his father or the other side's father as judge. That might be because a father is normally a valid judge for other people, so the agreement is easier to keep. One witness is never enough for anyone, so without our משנה we might think even the רבנן would let him back out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (both teachings are needed)
One like two (one witness treated as two)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Father' here is not about honoring parents. The next משנה deals with a litigant who says 'I trust my father' or 'I trust your father' to judge my case, and fathers are normally disqualified as relatives.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if it had taught 'my father' and 'your father' –
phrases.notes: This points to the next משנה, where a litigant says he trusts his father or the other side's father to judge.

phrases.english: in this case the Rabbis say
that he cannot back out of it,
because my father and your father are fit for the general public.
But one as two,
which is not fit for the general public –
I might say: they agree with Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי תְּנָא ״אַבָּא״ וְ״אָבִיךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why the argument is repeated in two משניות, now that רב דימי has defined our case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each teaching adds something the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without our משנה, we would think the רבנן agree with רבי מאיר that one can back out of accepting one witness as two.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה teaches that the רבנן hold he cannot back out even with one witness.

steps.title: Both cases are needed: our case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If we only had our case of one witness, we might think רבי מאיר agrees with the רבנן in the 'father' case, so both teachings are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had only taught us this case, we would say that only here does רבי מאיר rule he can back out. But in that case, of the father, you might say he agrees with the רבנן. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of the צריכא. Our case alone would not teach us רבי מאיר's view in the 'father' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר lets the litigant back out in our case. That might be only because one witness is never valid for anyone else. A father is normally fit to judge, so we might think רבי מאיר would hold him to that agreement. Each case teaches something the other cannot, so both are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught us / let us hear

steps.whatToRemember: The argument appears twice because each case could make us think one side agrees with the other. The 'father' case is a stronger case for the רבנן, and the one-witness case is a stronger case for רבי מאיר. Teaching both shows they argue in both.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us this case,
in this case Rabbi Meir says so,
but in that case –
I might say he agrees with the Rabbis.
It is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכא by showing the reverse side.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the next משנה, we would think רבי מאיר agrees with the רבנן that one cannot back out of accepting a father.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both משניות are needed so that we know the argument applies in both cases.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה says 'witnesses' in plural
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב דימי. The משנה says 'his judge' in singular but 'his witnesses' in plural, so it seems to mean exactly two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the first part teaches 'his judge' and the last part teaches 'his witnesses', it is clear that the wording is exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב דימי's explanation using the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה switches from singular ('his judge') to plural ('his witnesses'). That change suggests it was worded on purpose. So the witness case seems to be about two real witnesses, not one witness accepted as two, which goes against רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה

phrases.english: But since the first part teaches 'his judge',
and the last part 'his witnesses' –
this shows it is taught precisely.
phrases.notes: So 'witnesses' really means more than one, which is hard for רב דימי's 'one'.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי רֵישָׁא ״דַּיָּינוֹ״ וְסֵיפָא ״עֵדָיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב דימי's explanation from Step 1 and challenges it from the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that the case is one witness accepted as two
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה uses singular for the judge and plural for the witnesses. That contrast shows the wording is exact, so the case involves two witnesses, not one.

steps.title: The litigant and another person disqualify the witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the משנה is talking about a litigant who comes together with another person to disqualify the other side's witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The case is where he and another person come to disqualify them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר offers a new way to read the משנה, after the challenge to רב דימי in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, the משנה is not about the litigant agreeing to rely on one witness. Instead, it is about disqualifying the other side's witnesses. The litigant does this together with one more person, so there are two people testifying against the witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives this new explanation

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
It is where he and another come to disqualify them.
phrases.notes: "He" is the litigant, and "them" means the other side's witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: בְּבָא הוּא וְאַחֵר לְפוֹסְלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reading of the משנה after the challenge to רב דימי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to involve relying on a single witness or judge.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a litigant plus another person disqualifying the other side's witnesses.

steps.title: The litigant has a personal interest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: how can the litigant testify against the witnesses? He is personally involved in the case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it in his power? He has a personal interest in his testimony!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witness who gains from the outcome cannot testify. The litigant obviously wants the other side's witnesses thrown out, so his testimony should not count. That leaves only one valid witness, the "other person", and one witness is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it in his power? (Can he really do this?)
Someone with a personal interest in what he testifies, which makes his testimony invalid

phrases.english: Is it in his power?
He is an interested party in his testimony!

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל כְּמִינֵּיהּ? נוֹגֵעַ בְּעֵדוּתוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's reading, in which the litigant testifies against the witnesses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A litigant is נוגע בעדותו, so his testimony is invalid.

steps.title: He only raised a challenge against the witness
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא answers that the case is one where the litigant raised a challenge (ערער) against the witness. The next steps define what that challenge is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רב איקא, said: The case is where he raised a challenge against him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא defends the explanation from the problem of נוגע בעדותו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The litigant raises a challenge (ערער) that calls the witness's fitness into question. The גמרא has not yet said what the challenge is about. The next steps show that a theft claim still fails because of נוגע בעדותו. Only a claim of a family flaw works, and only for רבי מאיר: there the litigant testifies about the family, and the witness is disqualified indirectly.

keyTerms.meaning: רב אחא, son of רב איקא, the אמורא who answers
A challenge or objection against a witness's fitness

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika, said:
For example, where he raised a challenge against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁקָּרָא עָלָיו עַרְעָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem of נוגע בעדותו.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: a challenge rather than testimony
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The litigant was testifying against the witness, which is invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The litigant only raised a ערער, so his personal interest does not cancel it.

steps.title: What kind of challenge?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of challenge רב אחא is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: A challenge about what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for clarification. This short question sets up the next move, where it tests the possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ערער is too vague. Before the גמרא can accept the answer, it needs to know what the litigant is actually claiming about the witness.

phrases.english: A challenge of what?

steps.triggerLanguage: עַרְעָר דְּמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of רב אחא's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the content of the ערער is

steps.title: A theft claim runs into the same problem
steps.stepSummary: If the challenge is that the witness is a thief, the litigant is again a person with a personal interest, so the claim cannot count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is a challenge about theft, is it in his power? He has a personal interest in his testimony!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible meaning of ערער and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Claiming that the witness is a thief is really just testimony that he is disqualified. So the same objection from step 6 comes back: the litigant is נוגע בעדותו. Calling it a "challenge" does not fix the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility the גמרא will test)

phrases.english: If we say a challenge of theft,
is it in his power?
He is an interested party in his testimony!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא עַרְעָר דְּגַזְלָנוּתָא, כֹּל כְּמִינֵּיהּ? נוֹגֵעַ בְּעֵדוּתוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible meaning of ערער.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רב אחא's ערער as a claim that the witness is a thief
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A theft claim is really testimony, and the litigant is נוגע בעדותו.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new problem. It is the same objection as step 6, showing that a theft claim leaves us back where we started.

steps.title: The challenge is about the witness's family lineage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the litigant's challenge is a claim of a family flaw (פגם משפחה). רבי מאיר accepts it, since the testimony is about the family and the witness is disqualified on his own. The רבנן reject it, since the litigant is still personally involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the challenge is about a family flaw. רבי מאיר holds: these people are testifying about the family, and the witness becomes disqualified automatically. The רבנן hold: in the end, he has a personal interest in his testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the 'thief' explanation failed, the גמרא says the litigant's challenge is about the witness's family background. It then explains how רבי מאיר and the רבנן each view this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'this witness is a thief' is a direct attack on the witness, so the litigant's personal stake ruins it. Saying 'his family has flawed lineage' is testimony about the family, and the witness is only knocked out as a side effect. רבי מאיר says that makes it acceptable, but the רבנן say the litigant still gains from it, so he is still נוגע בעדותו.

keyTerms.meaning: A flaw in family lineage that disqualifies a person
Has a personal interest in his own testimony

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the first full explanation of the dispute in the משנה. It shows that indirect testimony is treated differently from a direct attack on a witness, at least according to רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Rather: it is a challenge about a family flaw.
phrases.notes: He claims the witness comes from a family whose lineage disqualifies him, for example one descended from slaves.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
these people are testifying about the family,
phrases.notes: 'These' means the litigant and the person who testifies together with him.

phrases.english: and he (the witness) is disqualified automatically.
And the Rabbis hold:
in the end, he has a personal interest in his testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: עַרְעָר דִּפְגַם מִשְׁפָּחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected 'thief' explanation from step 9 with a workable kind of challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the challenge is about lineage, not about the witness's own wrongdoing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenge was that the witness is a thief, which is a direct claim where the litigant's stake disqualifies him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The challenge is about family lineage. רבי מאיר sees it as indirect testimony and accepts it, while the רבנן still see the litigant as נוגע בעדותו.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the dispute is about two sets of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that רבי יוחנן explains the dispute differently. It is about a case with two sets of witnesses, and it depends on whether a litigant must prove the witnesses he claims to have.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: The dispute is about two sets of witnesses. רבי מאיר holds that a person must substantiate his claim, and the רבנן hold that he does not need to.
steps.whatsHappening: A new explanation of the משנה arrives from ארץ ישראל. רבי יוחנן says the dispute is about a case where one side claims he has two sets of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds צריך לברר: someone who says he has two sets of witnesses must actually bring them. So knocking out one set doesn't really help the other side, and he is not considered personally involved. The רבנן hold אינו צריך לברר: the first side could win with only the first set, so disqualifying it does help the other litigant, and that makes him נוגע.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a continuation of the family-flaw answer. It is a completely different way to explain the same מחלוקת in the משנה.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings from there.

phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The dispute is in a case of two sets of witnesses.
For Rabbi Meir holds: one must substantiate,
phrases.notes: Someone who says he has witnesses must actually show that they exist.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold: one does not need to substantiate.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בִּשְׁתֵּי כִּיתֵּי עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the משנה, in place of the רבי אלעזר / family-flaw line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is about two sets of witnesses and depends on whether a litigant must substantiate his claimed witnesses (צריך לברר).

steps.title: With one set of witnesses, everyone agrees he cannot disqualify them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds a limit: if there is only one set of witnesses, all agree that the litigant cannot disqualify them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with one set of witnesses, everyone agrees that he cannot disqualify them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his statement by limiting the dispute. With only one set of witnesses, there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there is only one set, disqualifying it would clearly win the case for the litigant. So according to everyone he is personally involved, and his challenge cannot count. The מחלוקת exists only when a second set is in the picture.

phrases.english: But in a case of one set –
everyone agrees
he cannot disqualify them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בְּכַת אַחַת – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין יָכוֹל לְפוֹסְלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the boundary of רבי יוחנן's explanation from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With only one set of witnesses, all agree the litigant cannot disqualify them.

steps.title: Rav Ami and Rav Asi ask about a case with only one set
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי and רב אסי ask רבי יוחנן what the law is when there is only one set of witnesses there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי and רב אסי said before him: If there is only one set there, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Two students question רבי יוחנן about the one-set case he just mentioned. Before any answer, the גמרא objects to the question itself in step 14, reworks it in step 15, and gives the answer in step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that with one set, everyone agrees the litigant cannot disqualify them. רב אמי and רב אסי seem to ask about that very case. The next step points out that this was already answered, so the question must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: They said before him (asked their teacher)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לְפָנָיו רַב אַמֵּי וְרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Ami and Rav Asi said before him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא כַּת אַחַת, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If there is only one set there, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לְפָנָיו רַב אַמֵּי וְרַב אַסִּי: אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא כַּת אַחַת, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the one-set case that רבי יוחנן described in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the law is when there is only one set of witnesses.

steps.title: How can they ask about one set of witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the question of רב אמי and רב אסי. רבי יוחנן already said that with only one set of witnesses, everyone agrees the litigant cannot disqualify them.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are asking about a case where there is only one set? But you already said: with one set, all agree he cannot disqualify them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by the question in step 13. רבי יוחנן already answered the case of one set, so there seems to be nothing left to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 רבי יוחנן said that when there is only one set of witnesses, both רבי מאיר and the רבנן agree the litigant cannot disqualify them. So a question about 'only one set' looks pointless. The question must mean something else.

phrases.english: There is only one set there?
But didn't you say:
But with one set of witnesses
everyone agrees he cannot disqualify them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא כַּת אַחַת? וְהָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the question asked in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The question of רב אמי and רב אסי about a case of only one set of witnesses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן already ruled on the one-set case, and all agree there, so the question as asked has an obvious answer.

steps.title: The real question: the second set turns out invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what the question really means. The litigant knocked out the first set because there were two. If the second set later turns out to be relatives or otherwise invalid, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is this: if the second set turns out to be relatives or invalid witnesses, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reworks the question so it makes sense. It now asks about the second set turning out to be invalid after the first set was already disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, a litigant may disqualify one set when there are two. If the remaining set is later found invalid, then in the end there was really only 'one set' that counted. So should the earlier disqualification be undone?

keyTerms.meaning: It turned out / was found to be
Invalid as witnesses for another reason

phrases.english: Rather,
if the second set is found to be
relatives or invalid, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, נִמְצֵאת כַּת שְׁנִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by giving the question a new meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about a case where only one set of witnesses ever existed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about two sets, where the second set later proves invalid, leaving only one set in the end.

steps.title: The first witnesses already testified
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the first witnesses already testified, so what was done stays done. Some say רב אשי gave this answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The first witnesses already testified. Some say: רב אשי said, The first witnesses already testified.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the answer to the reworked question. What happened with the first set stays in place, even though the second set later turned out invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'first witnesses' are the litigant and the person with him, who testified to disqualify the first set. When they testified, there really were two sets, so their testimony was valid at that time. Finding out later that the second set is invalid does not undo that testimony, so the first set stays disqualified. A second version gives the same answer in the name of רב אשי.

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוחנן, answering רב אמי and רב אסי.

phrases.english: The first witnesses already testified.
phrases.notes: The 'first witnesses' are the ones who disqualified the first set. When they testified, there really were two sets, so their testimony counted.

phrases.english: Some say: רב אשי said:
The first witnesses already testified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: כְּבָר הֵעִידוּ עֵדִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question as it was reworked in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: What happened with the first set already happened properly and stays in place. Later problems with the second set do not reopen it.
steps.whatToRemember: Once the first set was handled while two sets existed, the result stands, even if the second set later proves invalid.

steps.title: Is this the same dispute as רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי מאיר and the רבנן may be arguing about the same issue as רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they disagree about the same issue as the dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a comparison. It is about to quote another dispute that may match the dispute about disqualifying witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of two sets of witnesses looks like a person with two ways to prove his claim. The גמרא wonders whether this is the same question that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about. The source for their dispute comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Shall we say
that in the dispute of רבי
and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל they disagree?
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי מאיר and the רבנן from the earlier dispute about disqualifying witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא, בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that links the witness dispute to a different known dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן matches the dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Being judged by a document or by possession
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that a person who brings both a שטר and a חזקה to court is judged by the שטר, according to רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he is judged by the חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One who comes to be judged with a document and with a claim of possession is judged by the document. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: He is judged by the possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source of the dispute it just mentioned. This sets up the comparison to the witness case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person defending his claim to land has two proofs: a deed (שטר) and three years of possession (חזקה). רבי says the court judges him by the deed. So if the deed is found invalid, he loses, even though the חזקה alone could have saved him. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he is judged by the חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
One who comes to be judged
Ownership shown by holding the land for some time

phrases.english: As it was taught:
One who comes to be judged
with a document and with possession,
is judged by the document. These are the words of רבי.
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
He is judged by the possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַבָּא לִידּוֹן בִּשְׁטָר וּבַחֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source text for the dispute mentioned in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: a person with both a שטר and a חזקה is judged by the שטר. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: he is judged by the חזקה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי says the חזקה is worthless in general. The argument is only about which proof the court uses when the person comes with both.

steps.title: Can a person really be judged by his חזקה and not by his שטר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the wording of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, since it sounds as if the שטר is ignored.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this: is he judged by the חזקה and not by the שטר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion that questioned the wording of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Read plainly, his words say that the שטר does not count at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר is strong proof, so there is no reason a court would ignore it. The literal reading of "he is judged by the חזקה" therefore cannot be right. This prepares the corrected reading that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: "And we discussed it." The גמרא is recalling an earlier discussion of this ברייתא.
Presumed ownership that comes from holding and using land for a set amount of time.
A written document, here a deed of sale.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא from step 18 about someone who brings both a שטר and a חזקה.

phrases.english: By the חזקה and not by the שטר?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל quoted in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase "he is judged by the חזקה" in the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read literally, the phrase means the שטר is ignored, and that makes no sense.

steps.title: Read it as "even by the חזקה"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבן שמעון בן גמליאל to mean that the person can win even with the חזקה alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: even by the חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means the person can win with the שטר, and he can also win with just the חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שטר still counts. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is only adding that the חזקה alone is also enough. רבי disagrees and requires the person to bring the שטר he says he has.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather, say." This introduces a corrected reading.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Even by the חזקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem raised in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means that only the חזקה counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either proof is enough, so the person can win even with the חזקה alone.

steps.title: They argue about צריך לברר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about whether a person must produce every proof he claims to have. This completes the proposed link to רבי מאיר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we hold that they argue about whether one is required to substantiate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes setting up the suggestion from step 17. It names what רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל actually argue about, which makes their argument look like the one in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that someone who says he has a שטר must bring it, so the חזקה alone is not enough. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that he does not have to. The משנה's case of two sets of witnesses seems to raise the same question, so רבי מאיר and the רבנן would be arguing the same point.

keyTerms.meaning: "And we hold." This refers to something already established.
Required to substantiate, meaning he must actually produce the proof he claims to have.

phrases.english: And we hold,
that they argue about whether one is required to substantiate.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַיְימָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the exact point of disagreement, which completes the comparison suggested in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about whether a person must produce every proof he claims to have.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the shared principle that would tie the two מחלוקות together. The rest of the סוגיא tests whether that link really holds.

steps.title: No, רבי מאיר and the רבנן argue only within the view of רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the link. Under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל everyone agrees, and רבי מאיר and the רבנן argue only within the view of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, everyone agrees. They argue according to רבי: רבי מאיר follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that the two arguments are the same. It says the argument in the משנה happens only inside the view of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, no one has to produce every proof, and רבי מאיר and the רבנן would not argue at all. If we follow רבי, רבי מאיר agrees with him that the proof must be produced. The רבנן still disagree, and the next step shows how they can do that without arguing with רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: "When they argue," meaning the place where the argument really is.

phrases.english: No.
According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל,
everyone agrees and does not argue.
Where they do argue, it is according to רבי.
phrases.notes: "They" means רבי מאיר and the רבנן from the משנה.

phrases.english: For רבי מאיר holds like רבי.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא. אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed link between the two מחלוקות set up in steps 17 and 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי מאיר and the רבנן line up exactly with רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל both sides of the משנה would agree, so the argument cannot be the same one. It exists only within the view of רבי.

steps.title: How the רבנן can hold like רבי and still disagree
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain that רבי was strict only because a חזקה gets its strength from the שטר. One set of witnesses does not depend on another set, so even רבי would agree there is no need to produce the other set.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן can say to you: רבי said that only about a חזקה, which draws its strength from the שטר. But here, these witnesses do not draw their strength from the other witnesses, so even רבי agrees that one does not need to substantiate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the רבנן of the משנה can agree with רבי's rule and still rule differently. They point out that the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה only works when it comes with a claim of how the person got the land, such as a purchase with a שטר. That is why רבי says the person must bring the שטר he mentions. Each set of witnesses stands on its own, so the reason for רבי's rule does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: "He only said it as far as here." This limits a ruling to its original case.
From the strength of, depending on.

steps.whatToRemember: The two arguments are not the same. רבי requires the person to bring his שטר only because a חזקה depends on the שטר. Two sets of witnesses do not depend on each other, so even רבי agrees there is no need to produce the other set.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן are not arguing with רבי here. They agree with his rule and are only showing that it does not apply to the case of two sets of witnesses.

phrases.english: And the רבנן can say to you:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי הָתָם
phrases.english: רבי only said it there
about a חזקה,
since it comes from the strength of the שטר.
phrases.notes: Holding land alone proves nothing. It counts only together with a claim of how he got the land, here the שטר.

phrases.english: But here,
since these witnesses do not come from the strength
of the other witnesses,
even רבי agrees
that one does not need to substantiate.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the רבנן fit inside the view of רבי, which step 22 left open.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the two cases are different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone who holds like רבי must require producing the other set of witnesses as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי's rule rests on the חזקה depending on the שטר. Separate sets of witnesses do not depend on each other, so even רבי does not require the other set.
steps.whyThisMatters: The reason behind a rule decides how far it reaches. רבי's rule applies only where one proof depends on another.

steps.title: רבין begins reporting רבי יוחנן's explanation of the first clause
steps.stepSummary: רבין arrives from ארץ ישראל and starts quoting רבי יוחנן's reading of the dispute, beginning with the first clause (רישא) of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he said that רבי יוחנן said: The first clause...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new explanation. רבין begins quoting רבי יוחנן, and the line stops at the word 'the first clause', so the real content comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא has tried to explain the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן in other ways. 'כי אתא רבין' signals a fresh report from ארץ ישראל with a different approach. By saying 'רישא', רבי יוחנן shows he will explain the first clause of the משנה, where רבי מאיר says one side may reject the other side's judge.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing a teaching from there)
An אמורא who traveled from ארץ ישראל to בבל and brought back teachings
The leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל, whose teachings רבין reports
The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the full explanation. It only opens רבין's report, and the actual explanation of the רישא comes in the next words.

phrases.english: When Ravin came,
phrases.notes: He means he came down from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings with him.

phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The first clause
phrases.notes: This is the first part of the משנה, where רבי מאיר says each side can reject the other side's judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to רב דימי's report in step 11, רבין brings a different version of what רבי יוחנן said about the dispute, starting with the רישא of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן's explanation is introduced and focuses first on the רישא of the משנה. The ruling itself continues beyond this line.
